overrides.title: Scoard
overrides.description: Real-time NBA platform with live game tracking, play-by-play visualization, virtual court playback, and league statistics.
overrides.longDescription:
Scoard is a modern NBA score application designed to simulate the feeling of watching a game without watching the broadcast. It combines live scores, game clocks, schedules, standings, box scores, player statistics, and play-by-play data in a responsive interface.

The application turns play-by-play events into a visual experience through a virtual court, sequential event playback, shot mapping, smart notifications, and contextual overlays. Its data layer uses the NBA CDN first and falls back to the NBA Stats API when archived or incomplete data requires another source.
overrides.architecture:
Scoard uses the Next.js App Router with serverless API routes for date-based game lists, game details, play-by-play data, standings, and per-game SSE streams. Shared TypeScript types and NBA API utilities normalize responses before they reach the UI.

Live game pages use adaptive polling for game and play-by-play data, while the SSE pipeline exposes per-game updates in under 500 ms and reduces upstream API calls by 99%. The repository also documents an important deployment constraint: SSE poller state is held in process memory and is not shared across serverless instances.
features: Live scoreboard with scores, game clocks, quarters, team records, and active-game state
Interactive court visualization for 300+ play-by-play events per game
Adaptive game and play-by-play updates with NBA CDN fallback to Stats API data
Schedules, box scores, player statistics, league standings, and previous matchups
Responsive dark interface with Framer Motion animations and contextual game alerts

overrides.title: SmartAgriNode
overrides.description: AI-powered agriculture platform combining soil analysis, live crop recommendations, weed detection, and a real-time dashboard.
overrides.longDescription:
SmartAgriNode is a full-stack agriculture platform that combines machine learning, computer vision, IoT hardware, and a web dashboard. It helps users make data-informed decisions through crop recommendations based on soil and environmental inputs, while a vision pipeline identifies weeds in field images.

The project includes a React and Vite frontend, a FastAPI backend, Supabase authentication and storage, trained crop and weed models, an agricultural dataset, and hardware support for ESP32 sensors and an ESP32-CAM. The repository also includes setup documentation for the backend, frontend, models, database schema, and hardware flow.
overrides.architecture:
The system is split into a hardware layer, a FastAPI backend, and a React frontend. The backend exposes authenticated crop-recommendation, weed-detection, health, history, and device endpoints, while Supabase provides authentication, PostgreSQL data, storage, and row-level security.

Sensor requests use an asynchronous command queue: the frontend asks the backend to queue a command, the ESP32 polls for work, hardware results are posted back, and the frontend retrieves the latest data. Weed scans use the same command-driven approach, rotating the camera in 45-degree steps to collect eight images for a 360-degree scan before running YOLOv8 and ONNX processing.
features: Crop recommendations using soil NPK, temperature, humidity, pH, and rainfall inputs
YOLOv8 weed detection with PyTorch and ONNX Runtime model variants
Supabase authentication, PostgreSQL history, storage, and protected user data
ESP32 sensor and ESP32-CAM integration for asynchronous field data collection
React dashboard with soil, climate, crop, detection, and user-history views

overrides.title: Dexter
overrides.description: Mobile-first species identification app that turns live wildlife captures into collectible cards and repeatable progression.
overrides.longDescription:
Dexter is a mobile-first species identification app built around the loop of going outside, capturing a live image, identifying the organism, and adding it to a personal wildlife binder. The product combines real-world discovery with collectible cards, rarity tiers, challenges, streaks, XP, and leaderboards.

The application is designed for mobile browsers and uses a capture flow to send observations through a species-identification pipeline. Identified species are enriched with taxonomy, images, and descriptions before becoming cards in the user's collection. The interface uses a physical binder metaphor with themed tabs, card reveals, and progression feedback.
overrides.architecture:
DexE is a Next.js application organized around route-level screens, feature modules, reusable UI primitives, and Supabase server/client helpers. The primary flows live under the app and features directories: authentication and onboarding, wildlife capture, collection, challenges, leaderboard, and profile.

The capture pipeline combines Google Gemini species identification with GBIF taxonomy, iNaturalist and GBIF media, and Wikipedia descriptions. Supabase handles Google authentication, PostgreSQL data, image storage, and collection/progression state. Zod is used for typed validation, while Framer Motion drives card reveals, tab transitions, and rarity-specific feedback.
features: Camera-first wildlife capture flow for mobile browsers
AI-assisted species identification enriched with taxonomy and reference data
Collectible species cards with rarity tiers, XP, streaks, and profile progress
Challenges and leaderboard systems that turn observation into long-term progression
Supabase-backed authentication, storage, database state, and collection management

overrides.title: Dodo
overrides.description: Cross-platform habit tracker combining task planning, progress monitoring, reminders, and lightweight gamification.
overrides.longDescription:
Dodo is a habit and productivity platform designed to combine task planning and progress monitoring in one consistent system. Users can organize recurring habits, complete scheduled work, write notes, manage reminders, and track streaks and completion history.

The project delivers the same product domain across a React Native mobile client, a Next.js web client, and a FastAPI backend. A central scheduling and sync system keeps habits and notifications consistent across clients, while Supabase provides authentication and PostgreSQL persistence.
overrides.architecture:
DoDo is structured as a multi-client workspace. The `dodomobile` application uses React Native navigation, context providers, native notification integrations, and shared API services. The `dodoweb` application uses Next.js, Supabase authentication, screen-oriented components, and the same backend contract.

The FastAPI backend groups authenticated endpoints by domain: tasks, categories, habits, notes, notifications, sync, and authentication. Supabase stores the application data and applies row-level security policies. The backend also contains progression logic, incremental synchronization, encrypted user-authored content, and deployment configuration for the API.
features: Task planning with priorities, categories, deadlines, timers, completion, and undo support
Recurring habits with streaks, completion history, and progression tracking
Notes, preferences, profile settings, and authenticated account management
Cross-platform React Native and Next.js clients backed by one FastAPI API
Push notifications, incremental sync, Supabase persistence, and encrypted user content
